summary.text: A 72-year-old Saudi male with T1DM diagnosed at age 14 had ischemic heart disease after ACS in 2022, hypertension, hypothyroidism, peripheral neuropathy with reduced vibration sensation, and author-described early nephropathy and Stage 3a CKD. He was cognitively intact and independent, followed a low-carbohydrate diet, and walked 30 minutes three times weekly. Before pump use, his regimen included aspirin 81 mg, rosuvastatin 20 mg, candesartan 16 mg and thyroxine 75 mcg daily, insulin degludec 15 IU, and aspart three times before meals. Severe hypoglycemia six months earlier caused loss of consciousness and a two-day admission.

Hypoglycemia three to four times weekly, hypoglycemia unawareness and persistent glycemic variability during multiple daily injections prompted hybrid closed-loop Tandem t:slim X2/Control-IQ pump therapy. He had used FreeStyle Libre 2 for over four years; reported pre-pump TAR/TIR/TBR were 47/51/2%. A1C fell to 7.7% within two weeks. The narrative reports early TAR/TIR/TBR of 16/82/2%, which conflict with Figure 2 and remain review-only candidates. At three months, TAR/TIR/TBR were 15/83/2% and CV was 30.2%. Image GMI is distinct from laboratory A1C. Table ACR 1.48 mg/mmol conflicts with the narrative mildly elevated description.

Despite independent pump operation, prior carbohydrate-counting experience and demonstrated correct set changes, a language barrier contributed to an unintended insulin dose during one set change and severe hypoglycemia requiring hospitalization. The team removed the pump and temporarily used insulin pens until stabilization. The error has no stated date relative to the serial follow-ups. Safety actions advocated language adaptation and caregiver involvement during set changes, and provided additional training. Pump restart and discharge are not documented.
